title: Govern
overview: School executive leadership involvement is minimal, with ad hoc management oversight and undefined roles resulting in sporadic and undocumented cybersecurity practices.
Leadership and management oversight begin to take shape with some governance structures and risk management strategies emerging, though not systematically applied.
Governance and strategic plans are formalized, with clear cybersecurity risk mitigation expectations, contracts, policies, roles, and responsibilities established and communicated.
Leadership is proactive, with governance frameworks and oversight guiding well-defined and managed cybersecurity policies and practices across the school system.

Governance and oversight are deeply embedded and continuously improved, demonstrating high levels of efficiency, effectiveness, and adaptability in the school system's cybersecurity strategies, operations, and processes.

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Risk mitigation defenses are not clearly defined. Third-party data-sharing agreements are not formal. Sensitive data processes need improvement. Risk management decisions are not included in cybersecurity initiative planning.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Operational processes and responsibilities are consistent but mostly ad hoc or reactive. Some contractual data-sharing agreements with third parties are formalized. Sensitive data processes are not routinely measured or enforced.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND risk mitigation operations are documented. Third-party data-sharing agreements are formalized and meet legal, contractual, and regulatory requirements. Sensitive data processes are measured and enforced and include privacy and security requirements. Controls are in place to prevent loss, damage, or theft. Strategic plans address cybersecurity roles and responsibilities. Risk management decisions are understood through the mission, expectations, and contracts.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND performance controls are in place at department levels to measure and evaluate system-wide risk. Resiliency measures to anticipate, prepare for, and recover from cyber events are in place and are a priority. Regular cybersecurity assessments are conducted to verify optimal performance levels. Strategic planning and budget allocations are fueled by needs assessment data.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND strategic plans inform cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and risk management decisions. Controls in place are effective, systematic, and responsive. Fact-based, cybersecurity assessments are optimized based on an organization-wide analysis.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Risk Mitigation and Cybersecurity Planning: • Can you describe how your school approaches risk mitigation and cybersecurity planning without clearly defined defenses? • How does your school's approach to risk mitigation and cybersecurity planning impact your overall cybersecurity posture? Third-Party Data Sharing: • How are data-sharing agreements with third parties managed in the absence of formal agreements? • What challenges have arisen from the current approach to sharing data with third parties? Sensitive Data Processes: • What processes are in place for managing sensitive data, and how are these processes in need of improvement? • Can you provide examples of the difficulties you've faced managing sensitive data?

Consistency in Operational Processes: • Can you discuss how operational processes and responsibilities for cybersecurity are managed, despite being mostly ad hoc or reactive? Formalization of Data Sharing Agreements: • What steps are you taking to formalize contractual data-sharing agreements with third parties? • How have formal data-sharing agreements impacted your cybersecurity strategy? Management of Sensitive Data: • How are sensitive data processes managed, and what measures are in place to ensure these are routinely tracked and enforced?

Documentation of Risk Mitigation Operations: • Can you explain how you document risk mitigation operations and how third-party data-sharing agreements meet legal and regulatory requirements? Enforcement of Sensitive Data Processes: • How are sensitive data processes measured, enforced, and integrated with privacy and security requirements? • What controls are in place to prevent loss, damage, or theft? Understanding of Strategic Plans: • How do strategic plans address cybersecurity roles and responsibilities? • Can you describe how risk management decisions align with the organization's mission and stakeholder expectations?

Department Level Performance Controls: • How are performance controls implemented at the department level to evaluate system-wide risk? • Can you provide examples of how these measures have improved your cybersecurity posture? Resiliency Measures and Cybersecurity Assessments: • What resiliency measures are in place to anticipate and recover from cyber events? • How regularly are cybersecurity assessments conducted to verify performance levels? Strategic Planning and Budget Allocation: • How do needs assessment data influence strategic planning and budget allocations? • Can you discuss the current strategic planning process and its impact on cybersecurity initiatives?

Informed Strategic Planning: • How do strategic plans inform your organization's cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and risk management decisions? • Can you provide an example of how this approach has been beneficial? Effectiveness of Controls: • How do you ensure that controls in place are effective, systematic, and responsive? • Can you share insights from recent cybersecurity assessments? Organizational-Wide Analysis for Cybersecurity: • How is an organizational-wide analysis used to optimize fact-based cybersecurity assessments? • Can you discuss how organizational-wide analysis has led to improvements in your cybersecurity strategy?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: The organization’s risk priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions are not clearly defined. A comprehensive risk management strategy is lacking or nonexistent. Processes are not documented or aligned to support the architecture and strategic roadmap.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: The organization’s risk priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions are being developed. Processes to develop a comprehensive risk management strategy are being established and used to support operational risk decisions. Risk management is transitioning from reactive to proactive.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND risk management processes are documented and agreed to by organizational stakeholders. Risk management processes include cybersecurity risk objectives, activities, and outcomes. Supply chain risk management processes are defined. Tracked action plans include disseminating cybersecurity risks to stakeholders. The risk management strategy includes a documented communication plan.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND the shared risk management strategy and desired response patterns are culturally embedded and well understood. All stakeholders are committed to detecting and responding to changing tactics and techniques of cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND the risk management strategy is fully deployed without significant weaknesses or gaps across the school system. Processes and lessons learned are regularly shared with the education market sector community.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Definition of Risk Management Priorities: • How does your school identify and prioritize its cybersecurity risks without clearly defined priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions? Development of Risk Management Strategy: • What steps are being taken to develop a comprehensive risk management strategy in the absence of documented processes aligned with your architecture and strategic roadmap? Support for Operational Risk Decisions: • How do you support operational risk decisions without a clear risk management strategy or documented processes?

Development of Risk Management Components: • Can you describe the process of developing the organization's risk priorities, constraints, risk tolerances, and assumptions? • How are these components being integrated into your cybersecurity strategy? Transition to Proactive Risk Management: • What measures are you taking to transition risk management from reactive to proactive? • Can you provide examples of how these processes are being established? Support for Operational Risk Decisions: • How are newly established risk management processes used to support operational risk decisions within the school?

Documentation and Agreement on Risk Management Processes: • How are risk management processes documented and agreed upon by organizational stakeholders? • Can you discuss the inclusion of cybersecurity risk objectives and activities? Supply Chain Risk Management: • How are supply chain risk management processes defined within your risk management strategy? • What actions do you track to disseminate cybersecurity risks to stakeholders? Risk Management Communication Plan: • Can you elaborate on the communication plan for the risk management strategy? • How does the communication plan for the risk management strategy facilitate sharing information on cybersecurity risks across the organization?

Cultural Embedment of Risk Management Strategy: • How is the shared risk management strategy culturally embedded within the school? • Can you share how this understanding influences response patterns to cybersecurity threats? Stakeholder Commitment: • How do stakeholders demonstrate their commitment to detecting and responding to changing cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities? • Can you provide an example of this commitment in action? Strategic Response to Cybersecurity Threats: • How does the organization ensure all stakeholders are aligned and committed to the strategic direction for responding to cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities?

Deployment of Risk Management Strategy: • How is the risk management strategy fully deployed and integrated across the school system? • Can you discuss the absence of significant weaknesses or gaps? Sharing Processes and Lessons Learned: • How do you regularly share processes and lessons learned with the broader education market sector community? • How does this sharing impact your cybersecurity posture? Continuous Improvement in Risk Management: • How does the organization ensure continuous improvement and optimization of the risk management strategy? • Can you provide examples of how feedback from the community influences your risk management strategy?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Roles and Responsibilities for the development and implementation of data privacy and cybersecurity policies and practices need to be defined. Resources and budgets need to be allocated to meet cybersecurity and data privacy needs of the school system.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Cybersecurity processes are developing with roles and responsibilities for internal and external stakeholders being defined. A school system executive leader is identified as the person responsible for the development and implementation of cybersecurity policies and practices. Resources and budgets are being allocated, with basic needs identified to meet the cybersecurity and data privacy needs of the school system.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND processes that demonstrate cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for the internal and external stakeholders are defined, understood and documented. Designated staff maintain data privacy and cybersecurity policies. Resources are aligned and allocated system-wide to meet cybersecurity current and future needs. Human resource processes include onboard cyber training and regular training.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND system-wide cybersecurity governance includes cybersecurity awareness programs to influence behavior among the workforce to be security conscious and properly skilled to reduce risks to the school system. The TLE practice areas are reviewed annually and improvement initiatives are based on evaluation results.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND roles and responsibilities for detection are well-defined to ensure accountability. Governance processes are audited annually to assess federal, state, and local regulatory compliance. The school system is working toward or has obtained the TLE seal mark of distinction.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Definition of Roles and Responsibilities: • How is your school currently defining the roles and responsibilities for developing and implementing data privacy and cybersecurity policies and practices? Allocation of Resources and Budgets: • What steps are being taken to allocate the necessary resources and budgets to meet the school's cybersecurity and data privacy needs? Establishment of Cybersecurity Framework: • How do you plan to establish a framework for cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to enhance accountability and performance assessment?

Development of Cybersecurity Processes: • Can you describe how cybersecurity processes are evolving within your school, particularly in defining stakeholder roles and responsibilities? Executive Leadership in Cybersecurity: • Who is the executive leader responsible for developing and implementing cybersecurity policies and practices? • How has executive leadership's involvement in developing and implementing cybersecurity policies and practices impacted your cybersecurity posture? Resource and Budget Allocation for Cybersecurity: • How are resources and budgets being identified and allocated to meet the school's essential cybersecurity and data privacy needs?

Documentation of Cybersecurity Roles and Responsibilities: • How are your organization's cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for internal and external stakeholders defined, understood, and documented? Alignment of Resources with Cybersecurity Needs: • Can you discuss how resources are aligned and allocated system-wide to meet current and future cybersecurity needs? Incorporation of Cybersecurity in HR Practices: • How are human resource processes adapted to include cybersecurity training during onboarding and regular updates for staff?

Cybersecurity Governance and Awareness Programs: • How does system-wide cybersecurity governance incorporate awareness programs to influence security-conscious behavior among the workforce? Review and Improvement of Cybersecurity Practices: • Can you provide examples of how you review TLE practice areas annually and determine improvement initiatives based on evaluation results? Enhancement of Cybersecurity Skills and Awareness: • How are staff encouraged and supported to improve their cybersecurity skills and awareness through ongoing training and development programs?

Accountability in Detection Roles: • How are roles and responsibilities for detection defined to ensure accountability within the school system? Annual Audits of Governance Processes: • Can you discuss the annual audit process for assessing compliance with federal, state, and local regulations? • How does the annual audit process process impact your cybersecurity strategy? Achievement of TLE Seal Mark of Distinction: • Is the school system working toward—or has it already obtained—the TLE seal mark of distinction? • What steps are you taking to achieve the TLE seal mark of distinction?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: The school’s policies for managing cybersecurity risks are lacking. Policies are not documented, communicated, or enforced.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: The school’s policies for managing cybersecurity risks are being developed. Governance practice includes the approval of strategic direction and policy creation to support operational risk decisions. Risk management is transitioning from reactive to proactive.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND cybersecurity policies are documented and agreed to by organizational stakeholders. Risk assessment policies include identifying new threats, vulnerabilities, and conditions that may impact the system's security.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND policies for managing cyber risks are reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and the school's mission. All stakeholders are committed to detecting and responding to changing tactics and techniques of cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND policies for risk management strategy are fully deployed without significant weaknesses or gaps across the school. Policy updates and lessons learned are regularly shared with the education market sector community.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Establishment of Cybersecurity Policies: • Can you describe how your school currently manages cybersecurity risks without documented policies? Policy Communication and Enforcement: • Without established cybersecurity policies, how does the school communicate and enforce guidelines or rules regarding cybersecurity? Process for Developing Policies: • What steps are you taking to develop and implement cybersecurity policies within the school?

Development of Cybersecurity Policies: • How are the school's policies for managing cybersecurity risks currently being developed? • Can you share the process involved in policy creation? Governance Practice in Policy Approval: • What governance practices are in place to approve strategic direction and policy creation to support operational risk decisions? Transition to Proactive Risk Management: • Can you describe how risk management is transitioning from reactive to proactive within the context of policy development?

Documentation and Stakeholder Agreement on Policies: • How are cybersecurity policies documented and agreed upon by organizational stakeholders? Inclusion of Risk Assessment in Policies: • How do your risk assessment policies account for identifying new threats, vulnerabilities, and conditions that may impact system security? Policy Communication to Stakeholders: • How are documented cybersecurity policies communicated to relevant stakeholders within the school?

Review and Update of Cybersecurity Policies: • How are policies for managing cybersecurity risks reviewed and updated to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and the school's mission? Stakeholder Commitment to Cybersecurity: • Can you discuss the level of stakeholder commitment to detecting and responding to changes in cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities? Enforcement of Updated Policies: • How are updated policies communicated and enforced across the school to ensure compliance and adaptation to new cybersecurity challenges?

Deployment of Risk Management Strategy in Policies: • How is the risk management strategy integrated into cybersecurity policies to ensure no significant weaknesses or gaps exist across the school? Sharing of Policy Updates and Lessons Learned: • Can you explain how you regularly share policy updates and lessons learned with the broader education market sector community? Continuous Improvement of Cybersecurity Policies: • How does the school ensure continuous improvement and optimization of cybersecurity policies? • Can you provide examples of recent cybersecurity policy enhancements?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Lack of oversight in the review of cybersecurity guidelines, processes, or policy by executive leadership is evident. Cybersecurity risk management outcomes are not reviewed or adjusted to ensure coverage of school system requirements and risks.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Cybersecurity guidelines, processes, and policies are approved by executive leadership. Cybersecurity documentation undergoes review, evaluation, and improvement at a minimum annually. Cybersecurity risk management outcomes are reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of school system requirements and risks.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is measured and reviewed to adjust strategic direction. Cybersecurity documentation undergoes review, evaluation, and improvement quarterly.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND governance practices adhere to all federal, state, and local regulations.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND governance includes cybersecurity reviews conducted by an outside independent party on an annual basis.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Executive Oversight on Cybersecurity: • Can you describe how executive leadership is involved in the oversight of cybersecurity guidelines, processes, or policies within your school? Review and Adjustment of Cybersecurity Outcomes: • How does your school plan to implement oversight for reviewing and adjusting cybersecurity risk management outcomes to better meet system requirements and risks? Strategy Coverage: • Without current oversight, how does the school ensure the cybersecurity risk management strategy covers all necessary organizational requirements and risks?

Leadership Approval of Cybersecurity Measures: • How does executive leadership approve and oversee cybersecurity guidelines, processes, and policies? • Can you provide an example of this process in action? Annual Review of Cybersecurity Documentation: • Can you discuss the process and frequency of reviewing, evaluating, and improving cybersecurity documentation? • How does the current cybersecurity documentation review process impact the risk management outcomes? Adjustment to Ensure Coverage: • How are cybersecurity risk management outcomes reviewed and adjusted to ensure they cover all school system requirements and risks?

Measurement and Review of Performance: • How is organizational cybersecurity risk management performance measured and reviewed? • Can you share how these reviews have influenced strategic direction adjustments? Quarterly Review of Documentation: • What prompted the decision to review, evaluate, and improve cybersecurity documentation on a quarterly basis? • How has this frequency impacted your cybersecurity posture? Strategic Direction Adjustments: • Can you provide an example of how performance reviews have led to adjustments in your cybersecurity strategic direction?

Adherence to Regulations: • How do your governance practices ensure adherence to all federal, state, and local cybersecurity regulations? • Can you discuss any recent adjustments made to comply with federal, state, and local cybersecurity regulations? Impact of Governance on Cybersecurity: • How does the current governance model impact the overall cybersecurity risk management strategy and its effectiveness? Regulatory Compliance: • What processes are in place to continuously monitor and ensure your cybersecurity practices comply with evolving regulations?

Independent Cybersecurity Reviews: • How does having an outside independent party conduct annual cybersecurity reviews enhance your oversight and governance practices? Effectiveness of External Reviews: • Can you discuss the outcomes or improvements resulting from these independent cybersecurity reviews? How have they shaped your risk management strategy? Integration of Independent Reviews: • How are the findings from these independent reviews integrated into your cybersecurity risk management activities and performance evaluation?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to manage supplier risks are not documented and are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive. A comprehensive inventory of suppliers and third-party partners and the identification of the information systems, components, and services provided is lacking or nonexistent.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: An inventory of suppliers and third-party partners with processes to identify, assess, and manage supply chain risks is being developed. A systematic approach to evaluating third-party key processes is evident. Improvement initiatives with suppliers to ensure compliance are being developed.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND risk management processes include suppliers and third-party partners of information systems, components, and services. All processes are identified, documented, prioritized, and routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other forms of evaluations to confirm suppliers and partners are meeting their contractual obligations.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND suppliers and third-party partners conduct routine tests to evaluate compliance and the adequacy and effectiveness of all implementations. Results from tests ensure all policies, processes, and controls are managed as expected by ensuring the appropriate cybersecurity levels of control. Effective corrective actions are taken to address any weaknesses. Independent audits and valid certifications of proven performance are required.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND supply chain risk processes are advancing, optimizing, and progressive. Cyber defenses are maximized as evidenced by a comprehensive supply chain security program. Suppliers and partners are chosen based on risk and mission impact. Response and recovery planning and testing are conducted with suppliers and third-party providers at least annually. Results are evaluated and used for continuous improvement.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Supplier Risk Management Processes: • How does your school currently manage risks associated with suppliers and third-party partners without documented processes? Inventory of Suppliers and Third Parties: • How are you developing a comprehensive inventory of suppliers, third-party partners, and the information systems, components, and services they provide? Ad Hoc Supplier Risk Management: • Can you describe the challenges faced due to the ad hoc and reactive approach to managing supplier and third-party risks?

Development of Supplier Inventory: • How are you developing an inventory of suppliers and third-party partners? • Can you share the process and criteria for identifying and assessing supply chain risks? Systematic Evaluation of Third Parties: • What systematic approach are you using to evaluate third-party key processes? • How are you developing improvement initiatives with suppliers to ensure compliance? Initiatives for Supplier Compliance: • Can you discuss the initiatives being developed to improve compliance among your suppliers and third-party partners? • What measures are you putting in place to improve compliance among your suppliers and third-party partners?

Inclusion of Suppliers in Risk Management: • How are suppliers and third-party partners integrated into your risk management processes for information systems, components, and services? Routine Assessment of Suppliers: • Can you describe how suppliers and partners are routinely assessed through audits, test results, or other evaluations to confirm they meet contractual obligations? Documentation and Prioritization of Processes: • How are the processes related to suppliers and third-party partners identified, documented, prioritized, and assessed within your cybersecurity framework?

Routine Tests by Suppliers for Compliance: • How do suppliers and third-party partners conduct routine tests to evaluate compliance and the effectiveness of implementations? • Can you provide examples of these tests? Management of Policies, Processes, and Controls: • Can you discuss how you manage the results from supplier tests to ensure all policies, processes, and controls maintain appropriate cybersecurity levels? Corrective Actions and Independent Audits: • How are effective corrective actions taken to address weaknesses identified in supplier and third-party evaluations? • Are independent audits and valid certifications required?

Advancement of Supply Chain Risk Processes: • How are supply chain risk processes advancing, optimizing, and progressing within your cybersecurity framework? Annual Planning and Testing with Suppliers: • Can you discuss how response and recovery planning and testing are conducted annually with suppliers and third-party providers? • What improvements have been made as a result of response and recovery planning and testing with suppliers and third-party providers? Continuous Improvement Based on Evaluations: • How are annual planning and testing results with suppliers and third parties evaluated and used for continuous improvement in your cybersecurity supply chain risk management?

title: Identify
overview: Processes to identify cybersecurity risks are lacking or nonexistent.
Processes for cybersecurity risk identification exist but are in the beginning stages.
Risks to Information Technology (IT) assets are identified and managed in a standard, well-defined process.
Risks to the school system environment are identified and proactively monitored on a regular basis.
Cybersecurity risks are continuously monitored and used to make system-wide decisions.

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Asset inventory processes are ad hoc, inconsistent, and/or reactive and may be out of date. Controls for asset protection are lacking or need improvement.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Asset inventories are current and processes are consistent. Protection controls for asset protection are transitioning from being reactionary. Improvement initiatives are underway.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND asset inventories are current and document an asset's full life cycle. Data classifications are defined per state standards, regulations, and legal requirements. Protection controls are maintained and off-site asset security measures are in place, including software installs and asset transfers.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND asset inventory processes are highly managed with defined metrics. Effectiveness and accuracy are statistically analyzed. Asset compliance is evaluated regularly, and noncompliance is identified through root-cause analysis. Protection controls are tested, and results influence improvements.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND efficient, effective, and innovative asset inventories are in place system-wide with best practice process improvements. Inventory management is well integrated with the current and future needs aligned with system-wide objectives and risk strategy.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Ad Hoc Inventory Processes: • Can you walk me through how you currently manage your asset inventory? • How frequently is this information updated, and who is responsible? Protection Controls: • Can you describe the current controls for protecting your assets, including data, hardware, and software? • Have any instances occurred where you needed to test or improve these controls? Consistency and Reactiveness: • How do you respond when new assets are acquired or when existing assets are retired? • Is there a standard process in place when new assets are acquired or when existing assets are retired, or is it more of a case-by-case basis?

Current and Consistent Inventory Processes: • How have you standardized the process of maintaining current asset inventories? • Can you provide examples of how the process of maintaining current asset inventories has evolved from being reactive? Improvement Initiatives: • What specific initiatives are currently underway to improve asset protection controls? • How are asset protection control improvement initiatives being prioritized and tracked for success? Asset Protection Transition: • Can you describe the transition from reactive to more proactive asset protection controls? • What challenges have you faced in transitioning from a reactive to a proactive asset protection stance, and how have you addressed them?

Lifecycle Documentation: • How do you ensure that the asset inventories reflect the entire lifecycle of each asset? • Can you provide examples of how you use this information to manage assets? Data Classifications: • How are data classifications defined and maintained in compliance with state standards and regulations? • What processes do you have in place to ensure ongoing compliance with defined data classifications? Off-Site Asset Security: • What measures are in place for securing assets off-site, especially regarding software installations and asset transfers? • How do off-site asset security measures integrate with your overall security strategy?

Managed Processes and Metrics: • Can you describe how asset inventory processes are managed and monitored using defined metrics? • How do you measure effectiveness and accuracy? Asset Compliance Evaluation: • How often do you conduct evaluations for asset compliance, and what does this process entail? • Can you discuss how noncompliance issues are identified and resolved? Protection Controls Testing: • How are protection controls tested, and how do the results of these tests inform improvements in your asset management strategy?

System-Wide Integration: • How have you integrated inventory management with the broader system-wide objectives and risk strategy? • Can you give examples of how the system-wide inventory management integration has led to improvements? Best Practice Process Improvements: • What best practices have you implemented for managing assets more efficiently and effectively? • How do asset management best practices contribute to innovation within your organization? Alignment with Current and Future Needs: • How does your asset management approach align with both current and future organizational needs? • Can you describe how the alignment of your asset management approach influences decision-making and strategic planning?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Risk management capacity is lacking. Processes are not documented and are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive. Vulnerabilities are exposed and impacts are unknown. Collaborative approaches to risk identification and management are lacking or not evident.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Leadership demonstrates awareness of the importance of cybersecurity risk to organizational operations, assets, and individuals. The transition from a reactive to a proactive approach to risk management is evident. Processes to identify vulnerabilities and mitigate risks are being developed. Collaborative problem-solving and information gathering from information-sharing forums are being prioritized.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND processes to identify vulnerabilities, mitigate and minimize threats, and determine potential instructional and business operations impacts are documented and built into daily operations. Threat intelligence from information-sharing forums and sources is collected. Information processing facilities are secure. Processes for backup and recovery systems are documented, tested, and evaluated at least annually.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND established risk management strategy is in place with integrated improvements beyond compliance regulation requirements Priority is given to building knowledge about the risk management process and raising awareness about the needed capabilities to effectively conduct risk assessments and manage risk.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND risk assessment includes a focus on disciplined optimization and continual process improvement. Qualified cybersecurity practitioners are employed to measure and assess every aspect of the school system for possible cybersecurity issues and improvement opportunities. A fact-based evaluation cycle of improvement is optimized.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Documentation and Consistency: • Can you describe how risk management processes are currently documented and executed within the school? • How consistent are the risk management processes across different departments or areas? Awareness and Reactiveness: • How does the school identify and respond to cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities? • Can you provide examples of recent instances where risks were managed reactively? Collaboration in Risk Management: • What collaborative efforts are in place for identifying and managing cybersecurity risks? • How do you currently engage with external information-sharing forums or sources?

Leadership and Cybersecurity Awareness: • How has the school's leadership demonstrated awareness and prioritization of cybersecurity risks? • What steps are you taking to move from a reactive to a proactive risk management approach? Process Development for Risk Mitigation: • Can you discuss the processes being developed to identify vulnerabilities and mitigate risks? • How are the processes to identify vulnerabilities and mitigate risks shaping the school's approach to cybersecurity? Collaboration and Information Sharing: • How is the school prioritizing collaborative problem-solving and engagement with information-sharing forums? • Can you provide examples of how collaboration and information sharing have influenced your cybersecurity practices?

Integration of Processes into Operations: • How are processes for identifying and mitigating vulnerabilities integrated into the school's daily operations? • Can you give examples of how current processes for identifying and mitigating vulnerabilities affect decision-making? Use of Threat Intelligence: • How does the school collect and use threat intelligence from information-sharing forums and sources? • What impact has threat intelligence from information-sharing forums and sources had on your cybersecurity strategy? Security and Recovery Procedures: • Can you discuss the security measures in place for information-processing facilities and the processes for backup and recovery systems? • How often are security and recovery processes tested and evaluated?

Risk Management Strategy: • Can you describe the established risk management strategy and how it integrates improvements beyond compliance regulations? • How is the current risk management strategy communicated across the school? Knowledge Building and Awareness: • What initiatives are in place to build knowledge about the risk management process and raise awareness of necessary capabilities for effective risk assessments and management? Risk Assessment and Management Capabilities: • How does the school ensure it has the capabilities to conduct effective risk assessments and manage risks? • Can you provide examples of how risk assessment and management capabilities have been used recently?

Process Improvement and Optimization: • How does the school focus on disciplined optimization and continual process improvement in risk assessment? • Can you provide examples of recent process improvements and optimizations? Employment of Cybersecurity Practitioners: • Can you talk about how the school employs qualified cybersecurity practitioners to assess and improve cybersecurity across the system? • What impact have qualified cybersecurity practitioners had on overall cybersecurity? Evaluation Cycle of Improvement: • How is the fact-based evaluation cycle of improvement optimized within the school's cybersecurity strategy? • Can you describe how the fact-based evaluation cycle of improvement influences decision-making and strategic planning?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: An improvement posture is not evident or is lacking. Improvement is primarily reactive. The overall capacity for detection, response, and recovery is lacking or limited. Recovery planning alignment and coordination need improvement.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Improvement is beginning to transition from reactive to proactive. The overall capacity for recovery is limited but growing. Leaders demonstrate commitment to improvement. Budgets are being allocated to align the school system’s enterprise architecture and strategic roadmap to improve a comprehensive cyber recovery plan.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND actions taken to restore business continuity and protect assets after an incident are routinely analyzed. Improvement actions are identified as lessons learned for continuous improvement. Recovery plans incorporate retrospective (lessons learned) sessions and initiatives. Response and recovery strategies are updated.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND all stakeholders acknowledge the value of managing a pristine response and recovery plan. The school system evaluates incident response performance, identifies challenges, and improves incident response capabilities in strategic plans. Lessons learned and continuous improvement efforts result in an improved cybersecurity posture and readiness to face future security incidents.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND the school system continuously evaluates and improves response and recovery processes. Metrics are captured and used to evaluate processes and drive improvement. Advanced technology solutions are used to assist in all phases of incident recovery. Overall cybersecurity maturity and school system resilience improve through optimized incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery planning initiatives.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Reactive Improvement Efforts: • Can you describe any recent situations where you had to react to cybersecurity issues? • How did you address recent situations resulting in a reactive approach to cybersecurity issues, and what was the outcome? Capacity for Detection, Response, and Recovery: • What resources or systems do you currently have for detecting, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents? • How effective have detection, response, and recovery resources or systems been in past incidents? Recovery Planning and Coordination: • How do you plan and coordinate recovery efforts after a cybersecurity incident? • Can you provide an example of where the cybersecurity incident recovery process was challenged?

Transition to Proactive Improvement: • What steps are you taking to move from a reactive to a more proactive approach in managing cybersecurity risks and improvements? Leadership and Budget Allocation: • How has leadership demonstrated their commitment to cybersecurity improvement? • Can you discuss how budgets are being allocated toward cybersecurity improvement efforts? Aligning Architecture and Strategic Roadmap: • How are you aligning your school system's enterprise architecture and strategic roadmap to enhance your cybersecurity recovery plan?

Analysis of Recovery Actions: • Can you describe how incidents and the actions taken for business continuity are analyzed for improvement? • How are business continuity insights incorporated into planning? Lessons Learned and Continuous Improvement: • How do you capture and apply lessons learned from cybersecurity incidents to improve your processes and response strategies? Updating Strategies with Lessons Learned: • In what ways have your response and recovery strategies been updated based on retrospective lessons-learned sessions?

Value of Pristine Response and Recovery Plan: • How do stakeholders recognize the value of managing and continuously improving the response and recovery plan? Evaluating Incident Response Performance: • How do you evaluate the performance of your incident response? • Can you share how identified incident response challenges have led to improvements in your strategic plans? Improvements from Lessons Learned: • How have lessons learned and continuous improvement efforts resulted in a stronger cybersecurity posture and readiness for future incidents?

Continuous Evaluation and Improvement of Processes: • Can you explain how you continuously evaluate and improve your response and recovery processes? • What metrics do you use to drive response and recovery process improvements? Use of Advanced Technology Solutions: • How do you incorporate advanced technology solutions in your incident recovery phases? • Can you provide examples of how advanced technology has enhanced your incident recovery capabilities? Improving Cybersecurity Maturity and Resilience: • In what ways has your approach to incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery planning initiatives led to an improvement in overall cybersecurity maturity and system resilience?

title: Protect
overview: Asset protection is reactive and ad hoc.
Data protection techniques are implemented across the school system.
Data is formally defined and protected per its risk classification.
The school system environment is proactively monitored using protective technologies.
Protection standards are operationalized through automation and advanced technologies.

categories.name: IDENTITY MANAGEMENT, AUTHENTICATION, AND ACCESS CONTROL

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Access control processes and protocols for physical and remote access are not established and documented. Multi-factor authentication has not been implemented. Data protection measures are inconsistent. Network integrity processes are not defined. Account review processes for user, supplier, and system accounts are not defined. Conditions for group and role membership are not defined.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Access control processes and protocols for physical and remote access are documented but not routinely managed. At least one multi-factor authentication method is in place. Data protection measures are documented. Network integrity processes are defined. Account review processes for user, supplier, and system accounts are defined but not routinely enforced. Conditions for group and role membership are defined.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND compliant data protection measures are maintained. Network integrity processes, protections, and controls are routinely enforced. Account review processes are routinely conducted. Account managers are assigned. Conditions for group and role membership are routinely met.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND access control processes, protocols, and protection measures are systematic and well deployed. Multi-factor authentication methods are routinely evaluated for efficacy. Network integrity and account review processes are routinely evaluated for state and federal compliance. Evaluation processes include access control risk mitigation.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND data-driven decisions to mitigate and avert risk in alignment with best practices are routinely made. The overall approach to cybersecurity awareness, training, and implementation is fully deployed without significant weaknesses or gaps.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Establishment of Access Control Protocols: • Can you describe how your school manages physical and remote access control without established and documented processes? Implementation of Multi-Factor Authentication: • What measures are in place for user authentication, especially considering multi-factor authentication has not been implemented? Data Protection and Network Integrity: • How does your school approach data protection and network integrity without defined processes? • Can you provide examples of how you handle inconsistent data protection measures?

Documentation and Management of Access Controls: • Can you discuss the access control processes and protocols documented for physical and remote access? • How are access control processes managed? Use of Multi-Factor Authentication: • You've documented at least one multi-factor authentication method. How was this method chosen, and how is it implemented across the school? Definition and Enforcement of Account Review Processes: • How are account review processes defined for user, supplier, and system accounts? • Can you explain the challenges in routinely enforcing account review processes?

Maintenance of Compliant Data Protection Measures: • How do you ensure your data protection measures remain compliant? • Can you provide an example of how data protection measures are maintained? Routine Enforcement of Network Integrity Processes: • How do you routinely enforce network integrity processes, protections, and controls? • How do network integrity processes contribute to overall cybersecurity? Management of Account Reviews and Role Memberships: • How are account review processes conducted routinely? • Can you discuss how account managers are assigned and how group and role membership conditions are met?

Systematic Access Control Measures: • How are access control processes, protocols, and protection measures systematically deployed and managed within your school? Evaluation of Multi-Factor Authentication Efficacy: • How do you routinely evaluate the efficacy of multi-factor authentication methods? • Can you share insights from recent multi-factor authentication efficacy evaluations? Compliance Evaluation in Network Integrity and Account Reviews: • How are network integrity and account review processes evaluated for compliance with state and federal regulations? • What do network integrity and account review evaluation processes entail?

Risk Mitigation Decisions: • How are data-driven decisions made to mitigate and avert risks in alignment with best practices? • Can you provide an example of a data-driven decision-making process? Cybersecurity Awareness and Training Deployment: • How is the overall approach to cybersecurity awareness, training, and implementation fully deployed within your school? • Can you describe how you ensure there are no significant weaknesses or gaps in cybersecurity awareness, training, and implementation? Continuous Improvement in Cybersecurity Measures: • How do you ensure continuous improvement in your cybersecurity measures to stay aligned with best practices and mitigate risks effectively?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to ensure all staff and students with user ID accounts are undocumented and are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive. Cybersecurity awareness training is not mandatory or scheduled for new or existing users. Specific role-based security training to designated personnel is inconsistent or nonexistent. Personnel to document and monitor information system security training activities are not defined or designated. A records retention policy is not defined.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Processes are being developed to ensure all staff and students with user ID accounts are adequately trained. Cybersecurity awareness training improvement initiatives are being developed. Specific role-based security training for personnel with assigned security roles and responsibilities is defined. Personnel to document and monitor information system security training activities are identified. A records retention policy is defined.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND role-based security training is provided before authorizing access to the information system or performing assigned duties. Personnel to document and monitor information system security training activities are active in their designated roles. Training records are retained based on the records retention policy.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND regular cybersecurity alerts, training campaigns, and simulated attacks are issued. Staff and student training progress is routinely tracked and updated as needed based on available data. Leadership is involved in continuous process and training monitoring. Designated staff continually monitors, measures, and enforces training adherence.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND cybersecurity awareness and training methods are focused on continually improving performance through incremental and innovative optimization. Metrics to measure training performance objectives are established. A data-based evaluation cycle of improvement is optimized. Leadership is instrumental in designing, implementing, revising, and monitoring training initiatives and progress.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Cybersecurity Training Processes: • How do you currently address cybersecurity awareness and training for staff and students? • What challenges have you faced due to the lack of documented and consistent processes? Mandatory Training for Users: • How is cybersecurity awareness training handled for new and existing users in the absence of a mandatory or scheduled program? Role-Based Security Training: • What measures are in place for providing specific role-based security training to designated personnel, and how do you manage without consistent implementation?

Development of Training Processes: • What steps are you taking to develop processes ensuring all staff and students receive adequate cybersecurity training? Improvements in Cybersecurity Training: • Can you discuss the initiatives being developed to improve cybersecurity awareness training? • How are specific role-based training needs being addressed? Documentation and Records Retention: • Who is responsible for documenting and monitoring information system security training activities? • How is the records retention policy defined and implemented?

Role-Based Security Training Provision: • How is role-based security training provided before personnel are authorized to access the information system or to perform their duties? Activity Documentation and Monitoring: • Can you describe how personnel actively document and monitor information system security training activities? • How are training records managed according to the retention policy? Pre-authorization Training Requirements: • How do you ensure individuals receive necessary role-based security training before they are given authorized access or assigned duties?

Training Campaigns and Simulated Attacks: • Can you share how you integrate regular cybersecurity alerts, training campaigns, and simulated attacks into your awareness programs? • How is progress tracked and updated? Leadership Involvement in Training Monitoring: • How is leadership involved in continuously monitoring and improving the cybersecurity training process? Enforcement of Training Adherence: • How do designated staff monitor, measure, and enforce adherence to the cybersecurity training program? • Can you provide an example of how staff monitor, measure, and enforce adherence to the cybersecurity training program?

Continuous Improvement in Training Methods: • How are cybersecurity awareness and training methods optimized for continually improving performance? • Can you discuss the incremental and innovative optimizations you're making? Metrics for Training Performance: • What metrics do you have to measure the effectiveness of training performance objectives? • How are training effectiveness metrics used to drive improvements? Leadership's Role in Training Initiatives: • Can you explain how leadership is instrumental in designing, implementing, revising, and monitoring training initiatives and progress? • How does leadership involvement impact the effectiveness of your cybersecurity training program?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to manage and protect stored and transmitted data are not documented or are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive. Processes and policies to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and records are nonexistent or lacking. Leadership demonstrates an incomplete understanding of data protection and risk management.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Stored and transmitted data is managed and monitored consistently. Processes are defined, repeatable, and scalable. Leadership demonstrates sufficient understanding of data protection and risk management. Formal process definitions and protocol for managing and monitoring data and information are being developed and documented.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND data includes mitigating controls, protections, and innovative technologies. Data management and protection processes are routinely enforced. Data records are formally managed and are consistent with implemented risk management strategies. Exceptions for non-encryption are routinely evaluated. Dedicated technology staff monitors and investigates alerts.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND risk evaluation processes and measures extend beyond compliance requirements and regulations. Risks are routinely identified, analyzed, monitored, and controlled. Results from evaluation and monitoring processes and activities are used to drive improvements. Technology staff demonstrates a high degree of skill and knowledge in managing and monitoring stored and transmitted data.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND state-of-the-art data security solutions are used to provide enhanced visibility into system vulnerabilities. Innovative integrity-checking mechanisms are used to secure all information systems. Cybersecurity controls are adapted to meet the challenges of a dynamic information technology (IT) security environment. Technology staff demonstrates consistent ownership of proactive risk assessment and mitigation measures.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Data Management Processes: • Can you describe your current processes for managing and protecting stored and transmitted data? • What challenges have you encountered due to the lack of documented or consistent data protection practices? Understanding of Data Protection and Risk Management: • How does leadership currently understand and approach data protection and risk management? • Can you provide examples of how leadership's understanding of data protection and risk management impacts data security measures? Policies for Data Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability: • Without established processes and policies, how do you ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and records?

Consistent Management and Monitoring: • How are stored and transmitted data managed and monitored consistently in your organization? • What processes have you defined and implemented for managing and monitoring stored and transmitted data? Development of Formal Process Definitions: • What steps are you taking to develop and document formal process definitions and protocols for managing and monitoring data? Leadership's Understanding of Data Protection: • How has leadership demonstrated a sufficient understanding of data protection and risk management? • Can you give an example of how leadership's understanding of data protection and risk management has influenced data security practices?

Enforcement of Data Management Processes: • How do you ensure the routine enforcement of data management and protection processes? • Can you discuss any mitigating controls or innovative technologies you've implemented to enforce data management and protection processes? Management of Data Records: • How are data records formally managed, and how do they align with your risk management strategies? Monitoring and Investigation by Dedicated Staff: • Can you describe how dedicated technology staff monitor and investigate alerts related to data security? • How are exceptions for non-encryption evaluated?

Beyond Compliance Risk Evaluation: • How do your risk evaluation processes and measures extend beyond compliance requirements? • Can you provide examples of identifying, analyzing, and controlling risks? Improvements Driven by Evaluation Results: • How are results from your evaluation and monitoring processes used to drive improvements in data security? Technology Staff Skills and Knowledge: • Can you speak to the skill level and knowledge your technology staff demonstrates in managing and monitoring stored and transmitted data? • How does your technology staff's expertise contribute to your data security strategies?

Use of State-of-the-Art Data Security Solutions: • How do state-of-the-art data security solutions enhance visibility into system vulnerabilities within your organization? • Can you provide examples of your organization's state-of-the-art data security solutions in action? Adaptation of Cybersecurity Controls: • How are cybersecurity controls adapted to meet the challenges of a dynamic IT security environment? • Can you discuss the innovative integrity-checking mechanisms you use? Proactive Risk Assessment and Mitigation: • How does your technology staff demonstrate consistent ownership of proactive risk assessment and mitigation measures? • Can you share how your technology staff's proactive risk assessment and mitigation efforts have improved your organization's data security posture?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to maintain and repair information systems and applications in accordance with vendor specifications and requirements are lacking. Maintenance systems and tools are not controlled. Maintenance activities are primarily reactive and are sporadic and/or inconsistent. Security controls to verify functionality after maintenance lack definition. Records of maintenance activities are ad hoc, inconsistent, or incomplete. Processes to prevent unauthorized access need definition and/or improvement.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Systems and tools used to maintain and repair information systems and applications are routinely and consistently implemented per vendor specifications and requirements. Security controls are identified, documented, and implemented. Maintenance activity records are consistently kept. Processes are repeatable as the school system employs qualified “go-to” staff members for organizational knowledge. Formal definition and documentation of proactive and preventative maintenance activities are underway.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND documented processes to maintain and repair information systems and applications are implemented in accordance with vendor specifications and requirements. Maintenance systems, tools, and activities are approved, controlled, tested, and monitored. Post-maintenance security controls are routinely tested. Detailed records of maintenance activities are logged and retained. Remote maintenance of system assets is routinely approved, logged, and performed.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND maintenance of organizational information systems and applications is managed with acute care by designated, highly qualified staff. Regular maintenance is performed and verified to ensure all systems and components are effectively protected. Designated staff routinely monitors, measures, and enforces adherence to maintenance requirements and refresh cycles. The leadership chain of command is flexible to ensure resources are made available if there is a risk of noncompliance or poor performance.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND information systems and applications are implemented in a proactive life cycle of maintenance and repair. Continuous improvement focused on efficiency and effectiveness is optimized and flexible. Change management is strategically planned and consistently prioritized. Designated technology staff is thoroughly trained in cybersecurity and prioritizes routine, proactive system maintenance to meet and exceed security objectives.

interviewPrompts.prompts: System Maintenance and Repair Processes: • Can you describe how your school currently approaches maintaining and repairing information systems and applications without established processes? • How do you address information and application issues when they arise? Control of Maintenance Systems and Tools: • What challenges have you faced due to the lack of control over maintenance systems and tools? • How are maintenance activities typically handled? Security Controls and Maintenance Records: • How do you ensure the functionality of systems after maintenance activities, given that security controls lack definition? • Can you discuss how maintenance records are kept?

Consistency in Maintenance Systems: • How are systems and tools for maintaining and repairing information systems and applications implemented consistently across the school? • Can you provide examples of how system and application maintenance and repair are handled? Maintenance Activity Documentation: • What process do you have to keep consistent maintenance activity records? • How have security controls been identified and documented? Definition of Proactive Maintenance Activities: • Can you describe the steps to formally define and document proactive and preventative maintenance activities?

Documented Maintenance Processes: • How are documented processes for maintaining and repairing information systems and applications executed according to vendor specifications? • Can you describe the approval and monitoring process for maintaining and repairing information systems and applications according to vendor specifications? Post-maintenance Security Testing: • Can you explain how you routinely test post-maintenance security controls? • What procedures are in place for remote maintenance? Maintenance Records Management: • How are detailed records of maintenance activities logged and retained? • What impact has documentation related to maintenance activities had on your platform security?

Maintenance Management: • How are maintaining organizational information systems and applications managed to ensure protection? • Can you describe how regular maintenance is verified? Monitoring and Adherence to Maintenance Requirements: • How do designated staff monitor, measure, and enforce adherence to maintenance requirements? • What processes are in place for refresh cycles? Leadership and Resource Allocation: • How does the leadership ensure flexibility in the chain of command to provide resources for maintaining platform security, especially if there's a risk of noncompliance?

Proactive Life Cycle Maintenance: • Can you discuss how you maintain information systems and applications within a proactive life cycle? • What continuous improvement measures are in place for proactive information system and application maintenance? Change Management and Strategic Planning: • How is change management strategically planned and prioritized to enhance platform security? • Can you provide an example of how change management planning has improved efficiency? Training and Proactive System Maintenance: • How are designated technology staff trained in cybersecurity to prioritize routine, proactive system maintenance? • Can you share how your organization's technology staff training approach meets and exceeds security objectives?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to protect student and staff devices are lacking, or are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive. Advanced protective technologies to shield devices from identified and potential threats are lacking or nonexistent. Security updates are not conducted in a timely, scheduled manner. Time for information technology (IT) staff to capture and review audit logs needs is sparsely allocated or nonexistent. Additional protection measures for removable media and network infrastructure components are needed.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Processes to protect student and staff devices are being defined. Advanced protective technologies to shield devices from identified and potential threats are being researched and identified. Resources and budgets are being allocated. Qualified information technology (IT) staff are designated to maintain protection measures and security updates focused on ensuring the security and resilience of systems and assets. Protection measures for removable media and network infrastructure components are being determined.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND processes to protect student and staff devices are documented and implemented. Advanced protective technologies to protect devices are in place. Timely installation of security updates is applied. Audit log records are determined, documented, implemented, and reviewed in accordance with defined practices and policies. Removable media is protected, and use is restricted according to documented and implemented practices and policies. Communications and control networks are protected.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND the approach for implementing protective technologies is well deployed, with no significant gaps. Best practices drive performance levels, resulting in successful cybersecurity sustainability. Enhanced practices to protect changing tactics, techniques, and vulnerabilities of advanced persistent threats are reviewed and evaluated. Corrective actions are routinely taken to address identified weaknesses. Communications and control networks are routinely monitored. Automated checks are in place to avert cyber-attacks.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND the effects of deployed protective technologies are measured using key indicators. Evaluation results are used to guide improvement activities. Protective technologies are standardized across the organization. Processes are enhanced by using sophisticated protective technologies to detect and respond to advanced threats and vulnerabilities. Protective technologies aided by automated checks are resilient with an end goal in mind to ensure system availability and cyber protection is sustained at 100%.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Device Protection Processes: • Can you describe how your school protects student and staff devices without established processes? • What challenges have you encountered due to a lack of processes for protecting student and staff devices? Security Updates Management: • How is the scheduling and implementation of security updates handled, given their current status of needing to be conducted promptly? Removable Media and Network Protection: • What steps are you taking to address the need for additional protection measures for removable media and network infrastructure components?

Definition of Protection Processes: • How are you defining processes to protect student and staff devices? • Can you share how advanced protective technologies are being researched and identified? Resource Allocation for Security: • What resources and budgets are allocated to maintain protection measures and conduct security updates? • How are IT staff designated for tasks related to protecting devices and conducting security updates? Determining Protection Measures: • Can you discuss the steps being taken to determine protection measures for removable media and network infrastructure components?

Implementation of Device Protection: • How have you documented and implemented processes to protect devices? • What advanced protective technologies have been put in place? Management of Security Updates and Audit Logs: • Can you describe how timely installation of security updates is applied and how you manage the audit log records? Protection of Removable Media and Networks: • How is removable media protected, and how is its use restricted? • What measures are in place to protect communications and control networks?

Protective Technology Deployment: • How is protective technology implemented across your school's infrastructure to ensure there are no significant gaps? • Can you share how best practices drive your cybersecurity sustainability? Handling of Advanced Persistent Threats: • How are enhanced practices reviewed and evaluated to protect against changing tactics, techniques, and vulnerabilities of advanced persistent threats? Network Monitoring and Automated Checks: • Can you explain the routine monitoring of communications and control networks and the use of automated checks to avert cyber-attacks?

Measurement of Protective Technologies: • How are the effects of deployed protective technologies measured using key indicators, and how do these measurements guide improvement activities? Standardization and Sophisticated Technologies: • Can you discuss how protective technologies are standardized across the organization and enhanced with sophisticated technologies to detect and respond to advanced threats? Ensuring System Availability and Cyber Protection: • How do protective technologies, aided by automated checks, ensure system availability and cyber protection is sustained at 100%? • Can you provide examples of your organization's protective technologies in action?

title: Detect
overview: Anomalies and events are not detected or not detected in a timely manner.
Anomaly detection is established through detection tools and monitoring processes.
A baseline of normal activity is established and applied against tools and processes to better identify malicious activity.
Continuous monitoring of the cybersecurity program is established to detect threats in real time.
Detection and monitoring solutions continuously learn behaviors and adjust to detection capabilities.

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to actively manage all assets are nonexistent or incomplete. Processes to detect, remove, and/or remediate unauthorized and unmanaged assets are ad hoc, incomplete, or reactive. Reviews of accounts, firewall rules, and penetration tests of external-facing systems are not consistently conducted. External vulnerability scans are not performed at least quarterly.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Processes to actively manage assets are documented but are primarily reactive. A systematic approach to evaluation and improvement of key processes for detecting, removing, and/or remediating unauthorized and unmanaged assets is being formulated. Schedules for regular external vulnerability scans are being developed.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND processes to actively manage assets and to detect, remove, and/or remediate unauthorized and unmanaged assets are routinely implemented. Quarterly vulnerability scans are regularly conducted. Annual penetration tests are regularly conducted. Systematic account reviews are routinely performed.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND continuous monitoring processes to rapidly detect cybersecurity risks in real time are embedded in daily operations. Monitored performance of critical security processes using forensics, root cause analysis, threat intelligence, and incident response is prioritized. Effective correction actions are taken to address identified weakness or vulnerabilities.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND continuous security monitoring uses data to verify the effectiveness of proactive measures and optimizes real-time threat detection to aid timely mitigation, improve cybersecurity maturity, and reduce risk. Gap analyses via multiple technologies are conducted to identify vulnerabilities, develop failsafe measures, and drive process improvement.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Asset Management Practices: • How does your school manage and monitor its digital and physical assets? • What challenges have you faced in detecting, removing, or remediating unauthorized and unmanaged assets? Consistency in Security Reviews: • How often do you conduct reviews of accounts, firewall rules, and penetration tests of external-facing systems? • Can you provide examples of how your organization's security review practices might be inconsistent or reactive? External Vulnerability Scans: • Are external vulnerability scans part of your current cybersecurity practices? • If so, how frequently are they conducted, and what has been the outcome?

Documentation of Asset Management Processes: • Can you discuss the documented processes you have for managing assets? • How are you moving from reactive measures to more systematic approaches? Improvement of Key Processes: • What steps are you taking to evaluate and improve key processes for detecting and managing unauthorized and unmanaged assets? Development of Vulnerability Scan Schedules: • How are schedules for regular external vulnerability scans being developed and implemented? • What prompted the development of your organization's vulnerability scan schedules?

Routine Asset Management Implementation: • How are processes for managing assets and remediating unauthorized ones routinely implemented within your school? • Can you provide examples of asset management and remediation processes in action? Regular Security Assessments: • Can you explain how you conduct quarterly vulnerability scans and annual penetration tests? • How have scheduled security assessments impacted your cybersecurity posture? Systematic Account Reviews: • How are systematic account reviews performed, and how do they contribute to your overall security strategy?

Integration of Continuous Monitoring: • How is continuous monitoring integrated into your daily operations? • Can you describe the technologies and methods you use for real-time threat detection? Monitoring and Analysis for Security: • How do you prioritize the monitored performance of critical security processes? • Can you share how forensics, root cause analysis, and threat intelligence contribute to your incident response? Corrective Actions for Weaknesses: • When weaknesses or vulnerabilities are identified, what process do you follow to take effective corrective actions? • Can you provide an example of a recent improvement based on this process?

Effectiveness of Proactive Security Measures: • How do you use data from continuous security monitoring to verify the effectiveness of your proactive measures? • Can you discuss how security monitoring optimization has improved your threat detection capabilities?
