Gap Analysis for Vulnerability Identification: • How are gap analyses conducted to identify vulnerabilities? • Can you share how gap analyses have led—and continue to lead—to the development of failsafe measures and process improvements? Real-time Threat Detection and Mitigation: • How has optimized real-time threat detection aided in timely mitigation and reduced risk? • Can you provide examples of how your cybersecurity maturity has improved through real-time threat detection processes?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to collect, review, and correlate event data from a cybersecurity attack are not documented or are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive. A baseline of network operations and expected data flows for staff, students, and systems is nonexistent or lacking. Technology staff assigned to analyzing the impact of events are needed. The capacity to detect anomalies is lacking.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Anomalous activity is detected consistently but the approach is mostly reactive. Processes to collect, review, and correlate event data from a cybersecurity attack are being developed and improvement initiatives are being addressed. Technology staff are assigned to analyze the impact of events and the school system is transitioning from being reactionary. Staff are developing their skills in learning about pattern recognition and attack targets and methods.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND documented processes to collect, review, and correlate event data from multiple sources and technology systems are in place. A baseline of network operations and expected data flows is established and managed. Processes for collecting evidence and conducting forensic analysis are documented and in place. Designated technology staff routinely analyze the impact of events. Detected anomalies are analyzed via a formalized process. Pattern recognition technologies are used.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND rigorous analytics generated from anomalies and trends at the subprocess level of the school system’s applications, systems, and databases are used. Formal analysis is conducted of patterns of information technology activities outside of normal behavior. Underlying causes of vulnerabilities are identified through root-cause analysis. Issues related to vulnerability identification are tracked and reported to relevant managers.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND advanced processes generating immediate results are used to identify and detect anomalies and events and trigger rapid response. Cybersecurity technologies are based on threat intelligence combined with data analytics to segregate normal behavior from abnormal activity. Proactive technologies alert unauthorized access or suspicious behavior in real time.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Event Data Analysis Processes: • Can you describe how your school currently handles collecting, reviewing, and correlating event data following a cybersecurity attack? • What challenges have you encountered due to the lack of documented processes? Baseline Network Operations: • How do you manage and understand network operations and expected data flows without a baseline? • What impact has the lack of baseline network operations had on your ability to detect anomalies? Technology Staff Assignment: • What has been your approach to assigning technology staff to analyze the impact of events? • How do you cope with the lack of capacity to detect anomalies effectively?

Detection of Anomalous Activity: • How consistently is anomalous activity detected within your network? • Can you share how you are transitioning from a reactive to a more proactive approach to detecting anomalous network activity? Development of Event Data Processes: • What steps are you taking to develop processes for collecting, reviewing, and correlating event data from cybersecurity attacks? • How are improvement initiatives being prioritized for collecting, reviewing, and correlating event data from cybersecurity attacks? Skill Development in Staff: • How are staff developing their skills in pattern recognition and understanding attack targets and methods? • What training or resources are being provided to help staff develop their skills in pattern recognition and understanding attack targets and methods?

Documentation of Processes: • Can you discuss the documented processes for collecting, reviewing, and correlating event data from multiple sources? • How do processes for collecting, reviewing, and correlating event data from multiple sources improve your response to cybersecurity incidents? Baseline Establishment: • How have you established and managed a baseline of network operations and expected data flows? • What benefits has establishing and maintaining a baseline of network operations and expected data flows brought to your cybersecurity efforts? Evidence Collection and Analysis: • Can you explain your evidence collection and forensic procedures? • How do designated technology staff routinely analyze the impact of detected anomalies?

Use of Rigorous Analytics: • How are rigorous analytics from anomalies and trends used in your school’s applications, systems, and databases? • Can you provide an example of how analyzing anomalies and trends used in your school's applications, systems, and databases has identified underlying causes for vulnerabilities? Formal Analysis of IT Activity Patterns: • How is a formal analysis conducted on patterns of IT activities outside of expected behavior? • What has been learned from analyses of anomalous IT activity patterns? Vulnerability Identification Tracking: • Can you discuss how issues related to vulnerability identification are tracked and reported? • How do vulnerability identification processes inform your cybersecurity strategy?

Advanced Processes for Anomaly Detection: • How do advanced processes help you identify and detect anomalies and events to trigger rapid responses? • Can you share a recent example of when implementing processes for identifying and detecting anomalies was particularly effective? Integration of Cybersecurity Technologies: • How are cybersecurity technologies based on threat intelligence and data analytics used to distinguish normal from abnormal activity? • How has the integration of cybersecurity technologies affected your ability to proactively detect unauthorized access or suspicious behavior? Real-Time Alert Technologies: • Can you describe the proactive technologies in place that alert to unauthorized access or suspicious behavior in real time? • How have alert technologies enhanced your cybersecurity posture?

title: Respond
overview: Processes for responding to cybersecurity incidents are reactive or non-existent.
Analysis capabilities are applied consistently to cybersecurity incidents by Incident Response (IR) roles.
An Incident Response (IR) plan defines steps for pre-, during, and post-incident preparation, analysis, containment, and eradication.
Response times and impacts of cybersecurity incidents are monitored and minimized.
Detection and monitoring solutions continuously learn behaviors and adjust to detection capabilities.

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Approved processes to maintain a comprehensive cybersecurity incident response plan are lacking or nonexistent. Designated staff responsible for developing and implementing of the incident response plan have not been identified and/or trained.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: An incident response plan is documented. Improvement is a priority as evidenced in strategic plans. The beginnings of a systematic approach to the evaluation and improvement of key processes are evident. Appropriate staff are designated and trained to ensure a timely response to detected cybersecurity events.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND a comprehensive, formal cybersecurity incident response plan is documented and annually reviewed. Designated staff are responsible for participating in the development and implementation of the practices outlined in the plan. In-house and third-party scenario-based plan testing is routinely conducted. Results are systematically evaluated.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND a customized, scenario-based cyber event playbook is used to measure and evaluate risk. Business continuity, resilience, and agility are prioritized and incorporated in scenarios. Planning time is allocated to evaluate impact, response, and recovery. Practice is incorporated to strengthen recovery plans. Findings through practice are instrumental in generating action plans.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND the documented, reflective, flexible response planning process pervades organizational culture and undergoes continuous improvement on an annual basis, or more frequently where possible. Results from feedback drive change and aid retrospective (lessons learned) sessions and initiatives.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Incident Response Plan Status: • Can you describe the current status of your cybersecurity incident response plan? • How does the school handle incidents without a formal plan? Staff Responsibilities and Training: • Who is responsible for responding to cybersecurity incidents in your school, and what training have they received to manage these situations effectively? Process and Procedure Development: • What steps are you taking to develop and implement an approved process for managing cybersecurity incidents? • How are priorities set without designated staff or a formal plan to manage cybersecurity incidents?

Documentation and Improvement Priorities: • Could you walk me through your documented incident response plan? • How are improvements to the documented incident response plan prioritized in your strategic planning? Staff Designation and Training: • Who has been designated to handle cybersecurity incidents, and what training do they undergo to prepare for this responsibility? Systematic Approach to Evaluation: • What beginnings of a systematic approach do you have in place for evaluating and improving key processes within your incident management strategy?

Plan Documentation and Review: • How comprehensive is your cybersecurity incident response plan, and can you discuss the annual review process? • How are staff involved in the annual review process for the incident response plan? Scenario-based Plan Testing: • Could you provide examples of in-house and third-party scenario-based tests conducted? • How are in-house and third-party scenario-based test results used to improve your response plan? Staff Participation in Development: • How do designated staff participate in developing and implementing your incident response practices? • Can you describe the impact of the involvement of designated staff in developing and implementing your incident response practices?

Use of Cyber Event Playbook: • How does your customized, scenario-based cyber event playbook contribute to measuring and evaluating risk? • Can you share insights from recent scenario-based cyber event exercises? Incorporation of Business Continuity: • How have business continuity, resilience, and agility been prioritized and incorporated into your scenario planning? Findings and Action Plans: • Can you discuss how you use practice scenario findings to strengthen recovery plans and generate actionable improvements?

Reflective and Flexible Planning: • How is the reflective and flexible response planning process integrated into your organizational culture? • Can you provide examples of how the reflective and flexible response planning process has evolved? Continuous Improvement and Feedback: • How do you incorporate continuous improvement into your incident management process, and how are results from feedback used to drive change? Lessons Learned Initiatives: • Can you describe the lessons learned initiatives that have resulted from your incident management practices? • How have lessons learned initiatives impacted your overall cybersecurity posture?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to analyze incidents are insufficient. Adequate response and support for recovery activities are ad hoc, inconsistent, or reactive.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: A cross-functional process is employed to examine incidents. Systematic response and support for recovery activities are being developed. Proactive evaluation and improvement of key processes are being prioritized.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND incidents are analyzed and categorized consistently with response plans. Measures used in the analysis include compliance with federal and state regulations. Analysis findings and results are systematically evaluated. Additional third-party analysis is conducted.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND response analysis is culturally embedded and drives design, implementation, and evaluation. Detailed analysis is managed at the subprocess level to understand causation and correlation. Analysis drives processes identification and inventories for effectively mitigating risks and determining response levels.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND broad incident analysis is employed to identify shortfalls and performance gaps and drive process improvement. A team of knowledgeable information technology (IT) staff measures and assesses the full cybersecurity landscape, analyzing possible issues and identifying improvement opportunities.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Incident Analysis Processes: • Can you describe how your school currently approaches incident analysis? • How do you ensure effective response and support recovery activities without consistent incident analysis processes? Ad Hoc Responses: • In recent incidents, how have you managed to conduct investigations and support recovery efforts on an ad hoc basis? • Can you provide an example of how you investigated and responded to a recent cybersecurity incident? Consistency and Reactivity: • How do you identify the need to improve your incident analysis and recovery activities? • What challenges have you faced in improving your incident analysis and recovery activities due to the lack of consistent processes?

Cross-Functional Examination: • How does your cross-functional process work for examining incidents? • What cross-functionality process improvements are you currently prioritizing? Systematic Response Development: • Can you share how your school is developing systematic responses and support for recovery activities? • What role does proactive evaluation play in the process of developing systematic responses and support for recovery activities? Transition to Prioritized Improvement: • How are you transitioning to a more proactive evaluation and improvement of key processes in incident analysis and recovery? • Can you give an example of a recent shift from a reactive to a more proactive approach to incident analysis and recovery?

Consistent Analysis and Categorization: • How do you ensure incidents are analyzed and categorized consistently? • Can you discuss how compliance with regulations impacts your response plans? Systematic Evaluation of Findings: • How are analysis findings and results systematically evaluated in your school? • Can you provide an example of how systematic evaluation of findings has influenced your response to an incident? Third-party Analysis Contribution: • What role does third-party analysis play in your incident investigation process? • How does external analysis contribute to your overall incident management strategy?

Cultural Embedment of Response Analysis: • How is response analysis culturally embedded within your school? • Can you describe how embedded response analysis influences your incident management processes' design, implementation, and evaluation? Subprocess Level Management: • How do you manage detailed analysis at the subprocess level to understand causation and correlation? • Can you share how detailed subprocess analysis has helped mitigate risks? Analysis-driven Process Identification: • How does your analysis drive the identification of processes and inventories for effectively mitigating risks and determining response levels? • Can you provide an example of an improvement made based on analysis-driven process identification?

Broad Incident Analysis for Improvement: • How does broad incident analysis help you identify shortfalls and performance gaps? • Can you discuss how broad incident analysis leads to process improvement? IT Staff's Role in Cybersecurity Landscape Analysis: • Can you describe how your IT staff measures and assesses the full cybersecurity landscape? • How does your IT staff identify possible issues and improvement opportunities? Continuous Improvement Process: • How is the continuous improvement process integrated into your incident analysis and recovery strategies? • Can you provide an example of a recent continuous improvement initiative?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Processes to define orderly response activities are lacking or nonexistent. Criteria for incident reporting are not clearly defined or are primarily reactive. Communication processes for incident reporting are unclear or nonexistent.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Processes to define orderly response activities are being developed. Proactive coordination with internal and external stakeholders is improving. Consistent criteria for incident reporting is being determined. A systematic approach to evaluation and improvement of key processes is being designed.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND processes to ensure orderly response activities are defined and shared. Coordination with stakeholders is in line with response plans. Information is shared with leadership and internal and external stakeholders to achieve transparent situational awareness.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND processes are documented in a managed cybersecurity incident communication plan. Incident responsibilities are assigned to designated staff members. Defined criteria are used to measure the success of communications. Evaluation of the communication process is periodically conducted. Evaluation results drive tracked improvement initiatives.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND communications are optimized through collaboration with external cybersecurity and privacy groups, associations, and solution providers. Cybersecurity alerts and recommendations are obtained from and shared with external sources. Response activities are optimized using best practices, innovative processes, and technological aids.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Orderly Response Activities: • Can you describe how your school currently coordinates response activities following an incident? • How do you decide when and how to report incidents internally or externally? Incident Reporting Criteria: • What criteria do you currently use for reporting cybersecurity incidents? • How has your current approach to reporting cybersecurity incidents approach affected your ability to respond effectively? Communication Processes: • How are communication processes for incident reporting structured within your school? • Can you provide an example of a challenge you've faced due to unclear communication processes?

Development of Response Activities: • How are you developing processes for defining orderly response activities? • What steps have you taken to improve coordination with internal and external stakeholders? Criteria Determination for Incident Reporting: • How does your school determine consistent criteria for incident reporting? • Can you share how developing and implementing consistent incident reporting criteria has changed from a primarily reactive approach? Systematic Evaluation and Improvement: • What approach are you taking to systematically evaluate and improve key incident response reporting and communication processes?

Orderly Response Processes: • How have you defined and shared processes to ensure orderly response activities? • Can you give an example of how implementing processes to ensure orderly response activities has streamlined coordination with stakeholders? Information Sharing: • How do you ensure transparent situational awareness by sharing information with leadership and internal and external stakeholders? Stakeholder Coordination: • Can you discuss how your coordination with stakeholders aligns with your response plans? • How has coordination with stakeholders improved your incident response outcomes?

Cybersecurity Incident Communication Plan: • Can you explain how your cybersecurity incident communication plan is documented and managed? • How are incident responsibilities assigned? Success Measurement of Communications: • What criteria do you use to measure communication success following an incident? • How often do you evaluate processes for post-incident communication? Improvement Initiatives: • How do evaluation results inform your incident response reporting and communication improvement initiatives? • Can you share an example of an incident response communication improvement made recently?

Collaboration with External Groups: • How does collaboration with external cybersecurity experts, privacy groups, and solution providers optimize your communications? • Can you provide an example of how external insights have improved your response activities? Sharing with External Sources: • How do you manage cybersecurity alerts and recommendations with external sources? • How has information sharing with external sources influenced your incident response strategies? Optimization of Response Activities: • Can you describe how you've optimized response activities using best practices, innovative processes, and technological aids? • How have response activity improvements and optimizations affected your overall cybersecurity posture?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: A systematic approach to prevent the expansion of an event is lacking or nonexistent. Processes or technologies to mitigate the effects of and eradicate an incident are not defined, and practices are ad hoc, inconsistent, and reactive.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Processes for preventing the expansion of an event, mitigate its effects, and eradicate the incident are defined. The overall approach for cyber defense is consistent. Collaborative problem solving is used to prevent the expansion of an event.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND activities are routinely performed to prevent event expansion. Processes and technologies to mitigate the effects of and eradicate an incident are available and practiced. Incidents are contained. Identified vulnerabilities are mitigated and/or documented as accepted risks.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND sophisticated response mitigation during a cybersecurity incident is routinely managed using best practices, tools, and techniques. Effective mitigation is used to isolate and block threats in near real time. Processes are universally deployed and maintained to manage mitigation and generate data.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND risk mitigation activities and technical mechanisms are proactively and interactively improved. Roadmap development is prioritized. Leadership understands the importance of building resilience. Resources are made available when gaps in capabilities are identified. Vulnerabilities are cataloged and best practices are collaboratively established.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Systematic Approach to Incident Expansion Prevention: • Can you describe how your school attempts to prevent the expansion of cybersecurity incidents? • What challenges have you faced without a systematic approach to preventing incident expansion? Mitigation and Eradication Practices: • How do you currently approach the mitigation and eradication of incidents? • Are there any specific processes or technologies you use to mitigate and eradicate incidents, or is the approach more ad hoc? Consistency and Reactivity in Practices: • In what ways are your current practices for dealing with incidents inconsistent or reactive? • Can you provide an example of how inconsistent or reactive approaches to cybersecurity incidents have affected incident management?

Definition of Processes: • What processes have you defined for preventing the expansion of an event and mitigating its effects? • How did you arrive at your current processes for preventing incident expansion and mitigating the effects? Consistency in Cyber Defense: • Can you discuss how your approach to cyber defense has become more consistent? • What specific collaborative problem-solving techniques have you used to ensure cyber defense is more consistent? Event Expansion Prevention: • How do you collaborate internally or externally to prevent the expansion of cybersecurity events? • Can you provide an example of a recent cybersecurity incident and how it was managed to ensure it was contained?

Routine Prevention Activities: • What activities do you routinely perform to prevent the expansion of incidents? • How are routine incident containment activities integrated into your incident response plan? Containment and Mitigation Practices: • How are incidents contained and their effects mitigated with the help of available processes and technologies? • Can you walk me through a recent example of when processes and technologies were put in place to contain an incident? Vulnerability Mitigation Documentation: • How are identified vulnerabilities managed? • Are vulnerabilities mitigated immediately or documented as accepted risks, and under what criteria?

Sophisticated Response Mitigation: • How do you manage sophisticated response mitigation during cybersecurity incidents? • What best practices, tools, and techniques do you use for response mitigation? Isolation and Blocking of Threats: • Can you describe how you use effective near-real-time mitigation strategies to isolate and block threats? Universal Deployment of Processes: • How are processes universally deployed and maintained to manage mitigation and generate data? • How does data from response mitigation processes inform future incident response strategies?

Proactive Improvement of Mitigation Activities: • How are your school's risk mitigation activities and technical mechanisms proactively and interactively improved? Leadership and Resource Allocation: • How does leadership demonstrate understanding and commitment to building resilience? • Can you give an example of resources being allocated to address capability gaps? Cataloging Vulnerabilities and Establishing Best Practices: • How are vulnerabilities cataloged and best practices collaboratively established? • How do current processes for cataloging vulnerabilities and collaboratively developing best practices contribute to your school's overall cybersecurity posture?

title: Recover
overview: Processes for recovering from cybersecurity incidents are reactive or non-existent.
Resiliency and recovery capabilities are applied consistently to cybersecurity incidents impacting school system operations.
Continuity and disaster recovery plans define steps to continue critical functions, recover, and resume normal operations.
Recovery times and impacts of incidents are monitored and minimized.
The capabilities of all Information Technology (IT) personnel, processes, and technologies are regularly tested and updated.

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: Incident plans are nonexistent or lacking. Recovery action steps for educational continuity are not determined. If a plan is present, it does not align with strategic roadmaps or cybersecurity objectives.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Incident plans are documented. Recovery action steps describe restoration procedures with clearly defined roles and responsibilities. Plan execution is detailed in depth for during and after cyber incidents.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND asset protection, direct and indirect processes affecting normal operations. Evidence of plans being executed during or after cyber events is documented.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND incident plans are well managed. Pre-incident asset protection and recovery processes are routinely successful. Business continuity is tested. Leadership and information technology (IT) teams regularly review recovery processes. Gap analyses are completed with identified weaknesses translating to actionable improvement plans.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND fully integrated incident plans are embedded into daily decision making. Recovery planning is optimized using innovative techniques. Post-recovery (staged recovery planning or real-time cyber event recovery) includes addressing lessons learned and making improvements to the recovery plan. Leadership is committed to evolving strategic plans based on education market sector trends.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Existence and Quality of Incident Plans: • Can you describe the current state of your incident response plan, particularly regarding recovery actions for educational continuity? • How does your current incident response plan align with your strategic roadmap and cybersecurity objectives? Determination of Recovery Action Steps: • How do you determine the steps for recovery action in a cybersecurity incident? • Are recovery action steps documented or communicated within the school? Alignment with Objectives: • How have you managed recovery without a formal plan in cybersecurity incidents? • How do your current incident recovery approaches align with your school's broader objectives?

Documentation and Detailing of Incident Plans: • Can you walk me through your documented incident plan, especially the recovery action steps? • How are roles and responsibilities defined within the current documented incident recovery plan? Execution of the Plan: • How is your plan executed during and after cyber incidents? • Can you provide an example of a past incident and how the documented plan facilitated recovery? Clarity of Restoration Procedures: • Can you explain the restoration procedures outlined in your recovery action steps? • How do the restoration procedures outlined in your documented recovery action steps ensure the continuity of educational services?

Asset Protection and Normal Operations: • How do your recovery plans address asset protection and its impact on everyday operations? • Can you share evidence or examples of executed recovery plans in actual incidents? Documentation of Recovery Efforts: • How are your recovery efforts, including asset protection and direct and indirect processes affecting normal operations, documented and evaluated following an incident? Execution Evidence: • Can you provide instances of executed recovery plans during or after cyber events? • How were recovery actions documented and assessed for effectiveness?

Management and Success of Incident Plans: • How do you manage and assess the success of your incident plans, especially regarding pre-incident asset protection and recovery processes? Business Continuity Testing: • Can you describe how you test business continuity within your school? • How do leadership and IT teams review and improve recovery processes based on business continuity tests? Gap Analysis and Improvement Plans: • How do you conduct gap analyses of your recovery processes, and how are identified weaknesses translated into actionable improvement plans?

Integration and Innovation in Recovery Planning: • How are your incident plans integrated into daily decision-making? • Can you provide examples of how you've optimized recovery planning using innovative techniques? Post-Recovery Improvements: • How do you address lessons learned post-recovery, and what improvements have you made to the recovery plan based on these insights? Leadership and Strategic Evolution: • How is leadership committed to evolving strategic plans based on trends in the education market? • Can you give examples of how you've adapted recovery planning in response to education market trends?

levels.title: LEVEL 1: INITIAL
levels.description: A systematic approach for communicating restoration activities is lacking or nonexistent. Conditions and responsibilities under which the recovery plan is to be invoked are not defined or documented.

levels.title: LEVEL 2: REPEATABLE
levels.description: Processes are being developed to manage media interactions, handle and ‘triage’ communication requests, and ensure staff are apprised of public relations and privacy policies. Action steps to reduce damage inflicted by an event are defined. Communications include steps for handling data breaches and recovery activities.

levels.title: LEVEL 3: DEFINED
levels.description: Meets REPEATABLE Maturity Level AND conditions and responsibilities under which the recovery plan is to be invoked are documented. Communication about restoration activities and responsibilities is documented. Public relations, including reputation restoration after an event, are managed. Recovery activities are communicated to internal and external stakeholders, law enforcement agencies, and leadership teams.

levels.title: LEVEL 4: MANAGED
levels.description: Meets DEFINED Maturity Level AND a coordinated communication response to achieve a balance between the cybersecurity investigation and recovery is managed with concern. Communication channels are identified in advance. Communication templates derived from a playbook or tabletop exercises are described. Improvement initiatives are set forth based on the evaluation results from communication exercises.

levels.title: LEVEL 5: OPTIMIZED
levels.description: Meets MANAGED Maturity Level AND recovery communications undergo a continuous, cyclical improvement process and include a documented feedback and communication strategy. Feedback analysis identifies shortfalls or gaps in performance and drives measurable process improvement. Transparent communication is an integrated practice. A playbook with predefined communication topics helps to restore order and optimize the communication strategy.

interviewPrompts.prompts: Communication Strategy for Restoration Activities: • How do you currently communicate about restoration activities following an incident? • Is there a formal process or policy in place for communicating about post-incident restoration activities? Recovery Plan Invocation Conditions: • Can you describe the conditions under which you would invoke your recovery plan? • Are the conditions warranting execution of the recovery plan and the responsibilities associated with them documented? Systematic Approach Absence: • Without a systematic approach to communication, how have you managed communication regarding recovery activities in past incidents?

Development of Communication Processes: • What processes are you developing to manage media interactions and triage communication requests during recovery activities? Public Relations and Privacy Policy Awareness: • How do you ensure your staff knows and adheres to public relations and privacy policies during incident recovery? Action Steps for Event Damage Reduction: • Can you detail the action steps defined for reducing damage from an incident? • How do post-incident action steps include handling data breaches and recovery activities?

Documentation of Recovery Plan Conditions: • How are the conditions and responsibilities for invoking the recovery plan documented and communicated to relevant stakeholders? Management of Public Relations Post-Event: • How do you manage public relations and ensure your school's reputation is protected and/or restored after an incident? • How is the current process for managing public relations and protecting or restoring the school's reputation integrated with your recovery communications? Communication with Stakeholders and Law Enforcement: • Can you explain how you communicate recovery activities to internal and external stakeholders, including law enforcement and leadership teams?

Coordinated Communication Response Management: • How do you manage a coordinated communication response to balance cybersecurity investigation and recovery concerns? Pre-Identification of Communication Channels: • What communication channels have you identified in advance for incident recovery communication? • How do pre-identified communication channels facilitate effective communication? Use of Communication Templates and Playbooks: • Can you describe the communication templates and playbooks derived from tabletop exercises? • How have communication templates and playbooks been used in actual incidents?

Cyclical Improvement Process for Recovery Communications: • How does your recovery communication undergo a continuous improvement process? • Can you share examples of how post-incident recovery feedback is collected and analyzed? Integration of Transparent Communication: • How is transparent communication integrated into your incident recovery process? • What role does a playbook with predefined communication topics play in your incident recovery process? Measurable Process Improvement through Feedback Analysis: • Can you provide an example of how feedback analysis has identified shortfalls or gaps and led to measurable improvements in your recovery communication strategy?
